# Sourcera Audit — Defect Ledger

## Purpose

Authoritative, append-only findings store for the v7.1.0 production-readiness audit. Every finding produced by any audit prompt is recorded as one row in the `defects` table below. The ledger — together with `COVERAGE_MATRIX.md`, `CONSISTENCY_DELTA.md`, and `PRODUCTION_READINESS_VERDICT.md` — is the audit's source of truth.

The ledger is **append-only**. Do not delete defects; transition `status` instead.

## Row Format

The full row schema is defined in `/Sourcera/Audit_Prompts.md → Defect Ledger Format` (lines 49–68 of the v1.0 program). Reproduced verbatim here for in-place reference; if the two ever drift, the `Audit_Prompts.md` definition wins.

| Column | Definition |
|---|---|
| `defect_id` | `D-<phase>-<seq>` (e.g., `D-1.3-007`) **or** `D-<phase-mnemonic>-<seq>` (e.g., `D-AS-001` for Phase 1.1 Authoritative-Source Map sweep; `D-0V-001` for Phase 0 Verification). Sequential within a phase or mnemonic-bound sweep. The phase-mnemonic form is permitted to keep prompt-scoped ID strings stable across rolls of the phase numbering and to minimize cross-reference invalidation when a sweep spans more than one prompt within a phase. Once a defect_id is published, it is immutable; reroll via a forwarding row in this file if a renumber is genuinely required. (Amendment authority: defect `D-0V-007`, 2026-04-29.) |
| `severity` | `P0` / `P1` / `P2` / `P3` per the Severity Definitions block below. |
| `class` | `data_model` / `enum` / `glossary` / `rbac` / `acceptance_criteria` / `state_machine` / `api` / `webhook` / `notification` / `posthog_event` / `error_code` / `plan_gating` / `entitlement` / `numerical_singleton` / `retention` / `dsar` / `residency` / `firewall_leakage` / `surface_engine_mapping` / `ci_gate` / `consistency_drift` / `authored_extension` / `glossary_canonicality` / `accessibility` / `mobile_divergence` / `performance_budget` / `observability` / `test_coverage` / `instrumentation_gap` / `network_effect_gap` / `growth_mechanic_gap` / `documentation_gap`. Add a class only if every existing class is a worse fit; new classes go in this header. |
| `location` | Section anchor (e.g., `§4.4 → SellerSoftware`) or appendix reference. Include line-number range when relevant. |
| `summary` | One-sentence statement of the defect. Concrete and falsifiable. |
| `evidence` | Quote, line number, table cell, or cross-document delta. Must be reproducible. |
| `convention_violated` | The convention or contract the defect violates (e.g., `Master Spec authoring convention §4.1 — every entity must declare retention`). |
| `recommendation` | One-sentence proposed fix. If the fix is structural and large, link to a follow-up `RECOMMENDATION_<id>.md` artifact under `/Sourcera/_audit/`. |
| `remediation_owner_hint` | Default-suggested owner: `engineering` / `design` / `pricing` / `ops` / `security` / `legal` / `analytics` / `unassigned`. |
| `phase_owner` | The phase that found it (e.g., `Phase 1`). |
| `status` | `open` / `proposed_extension` / `wont_fix` / `remediated` / `superseded`. |
| `links` | Cross-references to related defects, Authored Extensions ledger entries, or `_integration/Decisions.md` rows. |

## Severity Definitions

Severity is rule-based, not vibe-based. Use the **first matching rule**. Reproduced from `/Sourcera/Audit_Prompts.md → Severity Definitions` (lines 72–83 of v1.0); if the two ever drift, the `Audit_Prompts.md` definition wins.

| Severity | Rule |
|---|---|
| **P0** | The defect blocks production deployment of v7.1.0 because it (a) breaks the buyer/seller console firewall, (b) exposes PII or PCI scope to an unintended actor, (c) violates a hard regulatory requirement (GDPR right-to-erasure, US/EU data-residency lock, audit-log integrity), (d) leaves a billing surface (AIOperation, AIWallet, OutcomeContract, Stripe metering) ambiguous in a way that allows revenue leakage or double-charge, or (e) leaves a CI gate referenced in `Build_Execution_Strategy.md` runtime-unwireable as written. |
| **P1** | The defect makes a feature unbuildable as written: missing field-level schema, missing acceptance criteria, missing state machine, missing error code, missing webhook contract, missing plan-gating row in §5.11/§34.1/§39, missing retention/DSAR/residency clause, conflicting numerical singleton between Master Spec and a companion strategy doc, or surface introduced without an Appendix-M row. |
| **P2** | The defect makes a feature ambiguous in a way that a thoughtful staff engineer could resolve, but the resolution is not the *same* across two readers (e.g., undefined edge case, soft-state behavior, sparse error-code coverage, accessibility gap that does not block compliance, mobile parity not specified, observability instrumentation under-specified). |
| **P3** | Cosmetic, terminological, or documentation drift that does not affect implementation but reduces spec hygiene (heading anchor missing, glossary entry duplicated, Appendix-J value listed but with stale comment, retired-document reference still present). |

**Tiebreakers.** When in doubt between P1 and P2, default to P1 if a junior engineer would build the wrong thing. Default to P0 only when the rule above explicitly applies — P0 is reserved for genuinely-blocking defects so that the production-readiness verdict reflects real shippability.

## Defect Statistics (Consolidation Pass — 2026-05-13)

> **Scope of this pass.** Deterministic ledger-wide enumeration of canonical defect rows (the 12-column `defect_id | severity | class | … | links` table). Counts cover every canonical row from `D-AS-001` to the V14 remediation block at the foot of the ledger. The pass also surfaces (a) the duplicate-candidate index, (b) the canonical-row-vs-supplementary-status-transition reconciliation gap. Per-defect content re-validation (severity rule-recheck, class specificity, evidence reproducibility, recommendation sharpness, link-column dedup, supersession marking) for 1,907 rows is a multi-session program; this consolidation pass delivers the deterministic statistics and the targeted hygiene findings below — the per-row content audit is staged as the v7.1.1 ledger hygiene backlog and is **not** complete inside this pass. The 517 supplementary rows under non-canonical schemas (status-transition tables, severity roll-ups, sign-off ledgers) are status updates against existing canonical rows and are excluded from the canonical-row counts.

> **Reproducibility.** Statistics were derived by parsing every row of the canonical 12-column table programmatically. Compound classes are normalized to their primary class (e.g., `data_model / residency` → `data_model`). Compound owner hints are normalized to the primary owner (e.g., `engineering + security` → `engineering`). Compound `Phase X.Y / (Prompt Z)` strings are preserved verbatim. The full raw counts (including compound-class long-tail) are reproducible against the canonical table at any time.

### Canonical-Row vs. Supplementary-Table Reconciliation Gap (P1 Ledger-Hygiene Defect)

The ledger holds **517 supplementary status-transition rows** distributed across post-line-639 remediation/verification sections under five distinct non-canonical schemas (5-column `defect_id | severity | status transition | landing location | verification`, 5-column `defect_id | severity | class | status transition | landing`, 4-column `defect_id | status transition | landing`, etc.). These rows transition existing canonical defects to `remediated` or `superseded`, but the originating canonical row's `status` cell has **not** been updated to reflect the transition.

Numeric reconciliation:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Supplementary status-transition rows total | 517 |
| Of which contain "remediated" | 337 |
| Of which contain "superseded" | 3 |
| Unique `defect_id` values appearing in supplementary tables | 433 |
| Canonical rows currently carrying `superseded` in `status` cell | 0 |
| Canonical rows currently carrying `remediated*` in `status` cell | 43 |

**Implication.** ≥ 390 canonical rows currently flagged `open` are actually `remediated` or `superseded` in the supplementary status-transition tables. The canonical-row counts above are therefore an overstatement of true open-defect inventory by roughly that margin. The reconciliation work — propagate each supplementary `→ remediated` / `→ superseded` transition into the originating canonical row's `status` cell and write a tight `links` reference back to the transition record — is staged as a v7.1.1 ledger-hygiene pass. The reconciliation cannot be silently executed inside this consolidation pass: each propagation requires the canonical-row author to (i) confirm the transition is closed, not partial; (ii) decide between `remediated` and `superseded` with rationale; (iii) update the row's `status` cell and append the transition citation to `links`. Filing one canonical defect against this ledger:

> **D-CONS-001** | P1 | documentation_gap | DEFECT_LEDGER.md canonical-row `status` column across all phases | Canonical-row `status` cells lag the supplementary status-transition tables; 0 canonical rows carry `superseded` despite 3 supplementary `superseded` references and ≥ 390 supplementary `remediated` transitions. | Diff of canonical-row `status` counts (open=1,863; remediated=41; superseded=0) vs. supplementary-table transition counts (337 `remediated`, 3 `superseded`, 433 unique IDs). | Ledger hygiene contract (this file §"Row Format" + Audit_Prompts.md §"Defect Ledger Format" — supplementary transitions MUST propagate to canonical rows). | Programmatic propagation script that walks each supplementary status-transition row, locates the originating canonical row by `defect_id`, and updates `status` + `links`; reviewer audit of each propagation; commit as v7.1.1 stamp gate. | audit + engineering | Phase CONS (Consolidation) | open | All supplementary status-transition tables under non-canonical schemas (lines 639–870, 1745–1804, 2435–2562, 2757–2820, 3094–3135, 3428–3460, 3700–3780, 4826–4990, 5264–5290, 5813–5860). |

### Outstanding Consolidation Work (Staged into v7.1.1 Ledger-Hygiene Pass)

Filed as P1 ledger-hygiene defects against this ledger; remediation owner is `audit + engineering`:

1. **D-CONS-001** — Propagate supplementary status-transition rows into canonical `status` cells (numbers above).
2. **D-CONS-002** | P2 | Per-row severity re-validation against the rule-based Severity Definitions block. Pass criterion: every P0 row's evidence cites one of the five P0-trigger rules verbatim; every P1 row's evidence cites a buildability gap; downgrade misclassifications.
3. **D-CONS-003** | P2 | Per-row class re-validation. Pass criterion: every row's `class` is the most-specific applicable class from the registered class set. Normalize compound classes — when the primary class accounts for ≥ 80% of the defect's substance, drop the compound and re-link the secondary axis via `links`.
4. **D-CONS-004** | P3 | Per-row evidence reproducibility audit. Pass criterion: every `evidence` cell contains a section anchor or line number; line numbers older than 2026-04-26 (v7.0.0) re-verified against current Master Spec lines.
5. **D-CONS-005** | P3 | Per-row recommendation sharpness audit. Pass criterion: each `recommendation` is one sentence (≤ 250 words) and proposes a concrete spec edit. Multi-sentence recommendations exceeding the cap are split into a follow-up `RECOMMENDATION_<id>.md` artifact under `/Sourcera/_audit/` per the row-format authority.
6. **D-CONS-006** | P1 | Per-cluster deduplication walk for the 78 duplicate-candidate clusters above. Pass criterion: each cluster reviewed; true duplicates merged with a forwarding row; partial overlaps cross-linked via `links`; one canonical row per actual defect.
7. **D-CONS-007** | P3 | `links` column completeness sweep. Pass criterion: zero canonical rows carry empty or `—` `links` after the sweep; every row carries at least one cross-reference (Authoritative-Source Map cell, Decisions ledger row, sibling defect, AE ratification row, or `n/a — first finding of class`).

D-CONS-001 through D-CONS-007 are filed as canonical defect rows below.

Failed login attempts are the canonical anomaly signal for credential stuffing, brute-force, and account-takeover (ATO). Excluding them from the audit log means: (a) no forensic trail when an account compromise is detected, (b) no SIEM-side correlation surface to detect impossible-travel or distributed-credential-stuffing, (c) no per-user audit history of who attempted to authenticate and when, (d) no compliance evidence for SOC 2 CC6.1 / NIST SP 800-53 AU-2 ("audit events shall include all successful and unsuccessful logon attempts"). §6.6.4 lines 27562–27563 document account lockout (5 failed attempts / 10 min → 15 min lockout) but emit NO audit event for the lockout itself or for the underlying failed attempts. §6.5 SSO and §6.6 password-auth flows emit zero audit events for any login outcome (success OR failure). The §51 PostHog taxonomy emits product-analytics auth events but those are NOT §4.6.1 AuditEvents — distinct retention, consent, and forensic-discovery semantics. P0 under rule (c) because exclusion creates a SOC 2 / NIST AU-2 finding regardless of actual security posture. | Master Spec line 9517 verbatim ("failed login attempts" excluded). | D-11.2-004 | P0 | ci_gate | Master Spec §M.4.4 override path (lines 49422–49428). | **Override-path bypass vulnerability.** The §M.4.4 override path auto-generates an "Internal-only, never surfaced" Appendix M.1 row when a `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation parses successfully (i.e., includes the required substring `internal-only construct, not surfaced`). There is NO cross-validation that the override target is actually an internal-only construct, that the named `{concept_name}` matches a concept the detector flagged, or that the rationale text is semantically truthful. An author can write `@appendix-m-internal-only: real_customer_visible_thing — internal-only construct, not surfaced (lie about it).` and the gate AUTO-PASSES, AUTO-GENERATES the Appendix M.1 row marked internal-only, and PERMITS MERGE. The "flagged for human review at the Phase 14.19 adversarial review pass" qualifier is post-hoc and post-merge. The merge has already shipped before review fires. This permits a customer surface to ship as a falsely-claimed-internal construct, which violates §M.2 process gate #6 ("a surface that appears for a tier listed in this column is a P0 defect") and §1.3 console firewall integrity (a buyer-only surface annotated `@appendix-m-internal-only:` could exfiltrate to a seller-console session without M.1-visible coverage). Severity is P0 per Audit Severity Rule (a) — "breaks the buyer/seller console firewall." | §M.4.4 line 49426: "When the gate parses a valid `@appendix-m-internal-only` annotation, it auto-generates the corresponding Appendix M row in §M.1 marked `Internal-only, never surfaced` with the rationale text appended in the Notes column, places the row under the appropriate spec-area group banner (inferred from the concept's spec anchor), and commits the row update to the PR branch as part of the gate run. (1) **Pre-merge cross-validation:** the gate MUST verify that the override target's `{concept_name}` matches a concept flagged by the detector in the same PR; an override for a concept the detector did NOT flag fails the gate with new status `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: override_target_not_in_trigger_set`. (2) **Pre-merge surface-class assertion:** the gate MUST run a static-analysis check that the concept's spec anchor does NOT introduce any of the surface-emission patterns (no new UI surface in §3.x / §11.x / §20.x / §22.20.x / §27.x / §29.x / §44.6.x / §50.x / §51.x; no new PostHog event in Appendix G; no new customer-visible webhook in §31). If the concept introduces a surface-emission pattern, the override fails with `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: override_target_appears_customer_visible`. (3) **Post-merge defense in depth:** the M.4.5 nightly digest aggregates `override_applied` runs and the reviewer SLA is bound to 24 hours from emission; review failure within SLA fires a SEV-2 PagerDuty page to a named on-call rotation. ### Phase 2 Strategic Findings

- **§2 vs §10 numerical drift was the single most consequential finding.** Remediated 2026-06-22 by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Method P1 pass: §2.1 and §2.5 now delegate phase names, phase-duration benchmarks, and total elapsed timeline to §10.15. Closed P1 rows: D-2-001 / D-2-013 / D-2-014 / D-2-015.
- **§2 acceptance-criteria absence is structural.** §2.1–§2.7 carry no numbered, testable acceptance criteria; only §2.8 (the v7.1.0 Phase 14.4 deliverable) has them. The Method-defining sections are the foundational contract for the spec, and their AC absence is a Method-wide P1 (D-2-042). Recommended remediation: author §2.x.N "Acceptance Criteria" sub-sections for §2.1–§2.7.
- **§2.8 Single-Operator Mode is dense but has 4 silent edge cases the audit prompt mandates as P1:** first-time vs returning operator (D-2-033); mobile divergence (D-2-036); concurrency on auto-team-transition (D-2-037); the Phase Advancement API extension is forward-referenced but not authored in §10.16.1 (D-2-028). Recommended remediation: author the missing edge-case behaviors against the existing §2.8.7 AC pattern, and update §10.16.1 with the v7.1 `soft_gates_enabled` request flag and `warnings` envelope.
- **Solo-Mode AE ratification gate is significant.** 22 `pending` AEs across Phase 14.4 / 14.6 / 14.9 face the v7.1.1 ratification gate per CLAUDE.md §16 (D-2-043). This is process backlog rather than buildability blocker; recommended remediation: schedule the ratification before v7.1.1 stamp.
- **§2.7 RFI/RFP framework lacks an entity model in §19.** §2.7 frames templates as RFI/RFP question structures while §19 frames them as Use Case + Requirement bundles; the relationship is unspecified (D-2-024). Recommended remediation: author a Buyer-side `template_kind` enum (`use_case_bundle`, `rfi`, `rfp`) on TemplateLibraryEntry and bridge §2.7 ↔ §19.

## Phase 12 — §12 Policy-Powered Requirement Generation

### Phase 12 Severity Roll-Up

- **P0:** 0
- **P1:** 13 — D-12-001, D-12-002, D-12-003, D-12-004, D-12-005, D-12-006, D-12-007, D-12-009, D-12-010, D-12-011, D-12-012, D-12-013, D-12-018, D-12-022
- **P2:** 9 — D-12-008, D-12-014, D-12-015, D-12-016, D-12-017, D-12-019, D-12-020, D-12-021
- **P3:** 4 — D-12-023, D-12-024, D-12-025, D-12-026
- **Total:** 26
- *(Counter note: 14 P1 rows above include D-12-022 which is P1 firewall_leakage; the listed enumeration totals 14 P1, 8 P2, 4 P3 = 26. Adjust the line above on next sweep if the cross-classification of D-12-022 is reconsidered.)*
- **Current P1 status (2026-06-23):** 0 open P1 rows remain in the D-12 cluster. D-12-002, D-12-004, D-12-006, and D-12-012 closed in v7.2.0-REM Phase 10; D-12-001, D-12-003, D-12-005, D-12-007, D-12-009, D-12-010, D-12-011, D-12-013, D-12-018, and D-12-022 close in the Phase 12 Policy Ingestion P1 pass. Lower-severity D-12 rows remain open unless independently remediated or status-synced.

### Phase 12 Strategic Findings

- **§12 is a v6.0.0-vintage section that never made the v7.x convention pipeline.** No PolicyDocument / PolicyControl entity in §4; no Appendix L state machine; no §32.5 endpoint cluster; no §31 webhook contract; no Appendix M.1 row; no §39 row coverage for any §12 numerical limit; no Appendix K glossary entries. The 13 P1 cluster is concentrated on missing convention blocks, not isolated drafting defects.
- **Plan-gating drift between §12.8.1 and §34.1.1 is the single highest-risk finding for Solo plan launch.** §12.8.1 has no Solo column (Phase 14.9), §12.8.2 inline cost ranges contradict §34.3.4's authoritative `policy_parsing` row, and §34.8.5's `business_starter` soft-gate conflicts with §34.1.1's "Free Allowance + Wallet" semantics for Free / Solo. A Free / Solo customer attempting Policy Ingestion has no canonical entitlement contract today (`D-12-011`, `D-12-018`).
- **Console firewall silence is a security-side P1.** §12 never declares Buyer-only scoping. A Seller-console caller hitting a Policy Ingestion endpoint must receive HTTP 404 per §1.3 / §7.2 — but no AC asserts this, no cross-reference binds §12 to the firewall doctrine, and the Cross-Console Bridge (§4.7) has no Policy Ingestion field enumeration (`D-12-022`).
- **Retention / DSAR / residency unauthored on regulated content.** PolicyDocument carries SOC 2 / HIPAA / GDPR / PCI material — exactly the content class with the highest retention and residency obligations — and §12 says nothing about any of it (`D-12-013`, `D-12-024`).
- **Deduplication algorithm is the most under-specified engine concept in §12.** §12.5 declares "embedding-based comparison" with a 0.90 threshold but no embedding model, no embedding storage, no merge transition table, no cross-framework merge semantics, no idempotency on resolution submission. Engineering cannot build §12.5 from the spec alone (`D-12-009`, `D-12-019`, `D-12-020`).
- **Amendment Protocol cite is broken.** §12.7.2 references "Section 10.3" which is "Phase 2: Requirement Definition", not the Amendment Protocol (§10.6 / §10.7 inline definition) (`D-12-023`).

**Phase-mnemonic.** Defect IDs in this prompt use `D-S17-NNN` (S = section-mnemonic; 17 = Master Spec section). Consistent with the `D-AS-NNN` / `D-0V-NNN` precedent established in `D-0V-007` (2026-04-29). IDs are immutable on publication.

**Self-challenge log.** After first pass: D-S17-001 promoted P2 → P1 (plan-gating row absent). D-S17-006 split — analytics-budget gap held P1, filter-latency duplication peeled off as D-S17-021 P2. ### Phase S17 Strategic Findings

- **§17 is the most under-specified evaluation surface in the buyer console.** No data model, no APIs, no PostHog events, no webhooks, no retention, no DSAR, and no §5.11 row-set despite §17 itself being one of the canonical AC-fidelity exemplars cited in Audit_Prompts.md ("§13.10/§14.9/**§17.8**/§20.7 style"). The exemplar is structurally weaker than its own §13.10 / §14.9 / §20.7 peers.
- **§51.1.5 self-contradiction.** §51.1.5 affirmatively claims "Every event documented in … §17 … is registered in Appendix G." With zero §17 events authored, the cross-reference table is false until either §17 instruments or §51.1.5 redacts §17. Recommend the §17 instrumentation path (D-S17-004) over redacting §17 from §51.1.5 — the latter would tacitly accept that §17 is not a customer-facing analytics surface, which contradicts the §17.1 Overview claim of "real-time and historical dashboards."
- **§44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment program left §17 untouched.** Phases 14.4 / 14.6 / 14.10 systematically applied surface compression to Pulse (§20), SLA Timers (§8.4), Inbox (§4.3.22), and divergence detection (§13.6.2) for `evaluation_owner_mode=solo` workspaces. §17 was not addressed. Recommend a §17.x Solo-Mode sub-section as part of v7.1.1 cleanup (D-S17-026).
- **Cross-Org "average" KPIs (§17.3.3 / §17.3.7) are the only un-walled cross-Org analytic surface in the buyer console.** Compare to §27.9.5 / §51.3 where cross-Org rollups apply k≥5 + residency partition + DSAR redaction. The §17 surfaces predate the v7.1 firewall doctrine and require remediation before v7.1.1 stamp (D-S17-014, D-S17-030).

## Phase 4 — Prompt 4.10 — §19 Template Library End-to-End Audit (2026-05-05)

**Scope.** Walk §19 (lines 14893–15095) end-to-end. Confirm the four prompt-mandated checks: (a) template versioning is authored to convention; (b) fork semantics are authored; (c) sharing permissions cite §5.11; (d) plan-gating cites §34. Walk every adjacent surface (§4.3 Buyer Console Entities, §4.4.28 TemplateLibraryEntry — the *other* "template" concept the spec uses, §5.11 Feature Access Matrix, §13.5 / §14.4 Amendment Protocol, §25 Cross-Console Bridge non-carry registry, §31 Webhook Catalog, §32.5 API Endpoints, §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.1.3 Plan Tier Definitions, §38.4 Mobile Parity, §39 Object Size Constraints, §40.2 Data Retention, §40.4 Data Residency, §44.5 Downgrade Behavior, §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment, §48.2.10 Loop L9 Template Publish Incentive, §49 Outage Catalog, Appendix C Notification Event Catalog, Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy, Appendix I Error Codes, Appendix J Controlled Vocabulary, Appendix K Glossary, Appendix L State Machines, Appendix M.1 Surface/Engine Mapping). Findings scratch log at `_audit/PHASE4.10_FINDINGS.md`.

**Verdict.** All four prompt-mandated checks FAIL. §19 is unbuildable as written against §4 / §5.11 / §32 / §34.1 / §40.2 conventions. The §19 surface introduces a "Custom Template" data class that has no §4 entity, no §32 API, no §31 webhook, no §5.11 row group, no Appendix K glossary entry, no Appendix J enum registrations, and a §19.6.1 plan-tier table that omits Buyer Solo / Seller Solo and conflates the buyer / seller plan-tier enums in a single column. 28 defects filed below — 11 P1, 13 P2, 4 P3. No P0: §19 does not break the buyer/seller firewall (§25 enforces buyer-only authorship explicitly), does not leak PII, and does not expose a billing-revenue ambiguity. The defect mass is concentrated at P1 (entity / API / webhook / audit-event / RBAC / Solo-tier) and P2 (edge cases — concurrency, idempotency, mobile, downgrade, residency, third-party outage, performance, surface-mapping coverage).

**Self-challenge withdrawals.** One defect (proposed `D-4.10-021` against §19.6.1 citing §34.4) was withdrawn on hostile-reviewer self-review: §34.4 covers customer-billed AI capability metering and "output artifacts are never per-unit billed" is a defensible read of that section. The remediation is consolidated into D-4.10-005 (numerical singletons).

## Phase 4 — Prompt 4.11 — §20 Inbox & Pulse End-to-End Audit (2026-05-05)

**Scope.** Walk §20 (lines 15099–15428) end-to-end. Confirm five prompt-mandated checks: (a) inbox aggregation; (b) Pulse health score math; (c) Pulse digest email cites §41; (d) Solo-mode suppression cites §44.6 and Appendix M.1; (e) mobile parity in §38. Walk every adjacent surface (§1.3 console firewall; §2.8 / §2.8.4 Single-Operator Mode contract; §4.3.10 Evaluation Pulse Event; §4.3.15 Unread Marker; §4.3.22 Inbox Item Group; §4.8.1 AIOperation; §5.9 Executive Sponsor; §5.11 Feature Access Matrix; §8.4 SLA Timers; §21.3 Agent Guardrails; §21.4.1 row #19 `pulse_digest_weekly`; §22.20 Seller Maya Surface Abstraction; §24.3 / §24.4 Seller Inbox / Seller Pulse; §29.1 Notification Event Catalog; §29.2 Delivery Channels; §29.3 User Preferences; §29.4 Slack Integration; §31 Webhooks; §32.5 APIs; §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 plan tier definitions; §34.10 AI Wallet; §38.4 / §38.8.2 Mobile Parity; §39 Object Size Constraints; §40.2 Retention; §40.4 Residency; §41 Email Deliverability; §44.1 latency budgets; §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment; §49 Outage Catalog; §51.3 / §51.4 Usage Dashboards; Appendix C / G / I / J / K / L / M.1). Findings scratch log at `_audit/PHASE4.11_FINDINGS.md`.

**Verdict.** All five prompt-mandated confirmation tasks FAIL. §20 is unbuildable as written against §4 / §29 / §31 / §32 / §34 / §38 / §41 / §44.6 / Appendix M.1 conventions. The §20.3.1 Pulse Health Score formula carries an inverted velocity-ratio term that systematically rewards slower workspaces; the §20.2.2 NotificationItem schema is irreconcilable with the §4.3.22 Inbox Item Group / §4.3.15 Unread Marker engine; the `pulse.health_score_threshold_breached` webhook cited in §2.8.4 / Appendix M.1 is unregistered in §29.1 / §31 / Appendix C / Appendix G; the `WorkspacePulseHealth` entity cited in §2.8.4 / Appendix M.1 has no §4 entity table; §20.4 does not cite §41 anywhere; §20 has zero references to `evaluation_owner_mode` / §2.8 / §44.6 / §22.20 / Appendix M.1 (the entire Solo-mode and Solo-tier suppression contract); §20 has zero references to §38; §20.6.2 names a phantom SMS notification channel with no §29 / §32 / §34 / §41 backing. 32 defects filed below — 0 P0 / 16 P1 / 14 P2 / 2 P3.

**Self-challenge withdrawals.** None. D-4.11-011 was consolidated to one row (vs. enumerating each missing endpoint) on hostile-reviewer pass; otherwise every drafted defect survived self-challenge.

## Phase 4 — Prompt 4.12 — §21 The Sourcera Agent End-to-End Audit (2026-05-05)

**Scope.** Walk §21 (lines 15433–15770) end-to-end. Confirm seven prompt-mandated checks: (1) Capability Registry (§21.4) is dynamic, no hardcoded 21 list; (2) Initial registry seed (§21.4.1) preserved; (3) Extended capabilities (§21.4.2) match §34.14 seller rate card and §34.15 outcome signals where applicable; (4) Platform-owned capabilities (§21.4.3) bill to Sourcera Marketing cost center; (5) Free-plan access rules (§21.4.4) match §34.4 / §34.10.3; (6) Outcome signals (§21.4.5) match Appendix L state machines; (7) Agent Budgets (§21.5) reference §34.10 AIWallet — no duplication. Walk every adjacent surface (§4.8.1 / §4.8.2 / §4.8.3 / §4.8.4 / §4.8.5 / §4.8.6 / §4.8.7 / §4.8.9 entities; §22.10 Managed Agents; §22.20.5 Seller Maya silent AI surface; §29 Notifications; §31 Webhooks; §32 APIs; §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.2.5 / §34.3.1 / §34.3.3 / §34.3.4 / §34.3.5 / §34.5 / §34.8.5 / §34.10 / §34.10.1 / §34.10.3 / §34.10.4 / §34.10.5 / §34.11 / §34.11.1 / §34.11.2 / §34.12 / §34.14 / §34.14.1 / §34.14.1.b / §34.14.6 / §34.15 / §34.15.1 / §34.15.1.b / §34.15.6 / §34.18; §39 Object Size Constraints; §40.2 Retention; §44 Performance Budgets; §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment; Appendix C / G / I / J / K / L / M.1). Findings scratch log at `_audit/PHASE4.12_FINDINGS.md`.

**Verdict.** Of the seven prompt-mandated confirmations, 1 PASS (#7 Agent Budgets ↔ §34.10 with no duplication), 3 PARTIAL (#1 Registry dynamic but `confidence_threshold_default` schema-gap; #4 Platform-owned mostly bill to Marketing but classification slips on placeholder rows; #6 Outcome ↔ Appendix L pass by inline-state-machine convention but bidirectional cross-links absent), and 3 FAIL (#2 Initial registry seed preserved but `capability_id` namespace drift across §21.4.1 / §34.14.1 / §34.3.4 / §34.11.1 leaves `kb_to_response_suggestion`, `qa_suggestion` family, and `first_pass_responses`/`first_pass_rfp_draft` triple-named; #3 Extended ↔ §34.14/§34.15 misses 8 AE seller capabilities entirely from §21.4.2; #5 Free-plan rules silent on Solo plans, mis-cite §34.10.1 vs §34.10.3 for Free pool definition, and audit-prompt's own §34.4 cross-reference is mis-anchored). 40 defects filed below — 0 P0 / 14 P1 / 18 P2 / 8 P3. - **AE Ledger touch points:** D-5.2-006 directly invokes an AE row (or row update) in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` for `kb_entry_draft_create` + `kb_dedupe_check` Authored Extension status. ### Phase 5.2 Counterfactual Pass

For each §22.1–§22.8 surface audited, three realistic failure modes were enumerated and the spec was checked against each:

- **Vault JWT expiration mid-session** — handled per §22.8.6 (orchestrator monitors `expires_at − now < 5min`; refresh path defined).
- **Anthropic MCP proxy outage** — handled per §22.8.6 (5s/30s/5m/30m backoff; AIOperation rejected with `mcp_proxy_unavailable` after 4 failures).
- **Race between namespace migration and active retrieval** — handled per §22.8.6 (migration sets `is_archived=true` before rewriting entries; in-flight calls filter the archived namespace).
- **One-time-use token replay attack** — handled per §22.8.3.1 (`jti` unique within `(org_id)`).
- **Cross-region token presented to wrong-region MCP server** — handled per §22.8.6 (HTTP 403 `wrong_region`).
- **Voyage embedding outage** — handled per §22.8.6 (BM25-only fallback with `degraded_mode=true` flag).
- **OpenSearch outage** — handled per §22.8.6 (dense-only fallback with same flag).
- **Both Voyage and OpenSearch out** — handled per §22.8.6 (HTTP 503 `retrieval_unavailable`).
- **Concurrent SellerSoftware deletions** — handled per §22.4.4 (per-Org pessimistic lock).
- **Edit during in-flight cite_verify call** — handled per §22.4.3 (`entry_modified_after_offset_capture` reason).
- **Persistent vectorization failure** — handled per §22.4.2 (auto-flag-stale after 5 retries).
- **Doc transitions to expired between find and attach** — handled per §22.7 (`doc_no_longer_active` error from `doc_attach`).
- **Bid Workspace force-closed mid-session** — handled per §22.8.3.1 (`revoked_reason=bid_workspace_closed`).

No additional unhandled failure-modes detected in §22.1–§22.8 scope. Out-of-scope items noted (deferred to v7.1.1 backlog if not already): Org-residency migration mid-session (§6/§40 territory).

For each §22.9–§22.20 surface audited, three realistic failure modes were enumerated and the spec was checked against each. Detailed in `_audit/PHASE5.3_FINDINGS.md → Counterfactual Pass`. Two unhandled failure modes promoted to defects:

- **§22.20.5 Solo / Free billing-API surface leak** — surface compression is UI-only; the §32.8 billing API can still return `cost_priced_rejected_cents_accumulated` to a Solo / Free seller's API key. → D-5.3-024.

All other counterfactual modes (Voyage outage, OpenSearch corruption, agent prompt > 8K, environment retention race, SSE disconnect, compaction storm, evidence < 3, SIM quarantine, hallucination spike, prompt-injection ingestion, etc.) are handled by the respective §22.9.9 / §22.10.8 / §22.11.4 / §22.12.10 / §22.13.4 / §22.14.7 / §22.15.5 / §22.16.6 / §22.16.7 / §22.20.7 failure-mode blocks.

### Phase 23 Counterfactual Pass

For each §23 surface audited, three realistic failure modes were enumerated and the spec was checked against each. Promoted to defects:

- **Bid Workspace lifecycle.** (1) Vendor accepts NDA but Bid Workspace materialization race fails — §4.7.1 retry curve covers; §23 silent on visibility (folded into D-23-005). (2) Bid Owner deactivated mid-bid — §23 silent on role re-assignment (D-23-008). (3) Phase 13 closes parent Workspace while Bid Workspace is `submitted` — Appendix E declares `submitted → closed`; cross-references intact (no defect needed).
- **Response submission.** (1) Loops.so outage during buyer notification of submission — no notification retry curve in §23 (D-23-020). (2) Wallet-empty during evidence cross-reference Agent run — §23 silent on degradation (D-23-019). (3) Bulk submit interrupted mid-cascade by network failure — §23 silent on idempotency (D-23-018, D-23-028).
- **Withdrawal.** (1) Withdrawal during in-flight Managed Agent session — §23 silent on agent termination (D-23-005). (2) Withdrawal racing buyer disqualification — §23 silent on conflict resolution (D-23-005, D-23-029). (3) Withdrawal during Phase 9 (responses already locked) — §23 says responses "remain in the system" but does not specify lock_reason or scoring exclusion (D-23-005).
- **Editor lock.** (1) User A goes offline before lock expiry — heartbeat / browser-close behavior unspecified (D-23-009 / D-23-010 cover the gap). (2) Force-release race between two contributors — RBAC unspecified (D-23-013). (3) Network partition at first-write-wins moment — error code unregistered (D-23-011).

### Phase 23 Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read 31 findings as a hostile reviewer. Severity reclassifications considered:

- D-23-001 / D-23-002 / D-23-014 — held at **P1**: junior would build one of the three contradicting state models at random; canonical resolution is required pre-implementation. Considered for P0 (firewall implication) and rejected — the enums are workflow states, not firewall fields.
- D-23-003 / D-23-004 / D-23-005 / D-23-009 / D-23-010 / D-23-013 / D-23-019 / D-23-020 / D-23-021 — held at **P1** (feature unbuildable as written: missing endpoint, missing webhook, missing schema, missing RBAC, missing entitlement, missing plan gating).
- D-23-006 — held at **P1**: missing audit-trail contract on a high-impact mutation (forensic reconstruction is mandatory per §25.3.5 precedent). Considered P0 (audit-log integrity) per the P0 rule (c); rejected because the existing system audit log fires *some* row on the underlying Bid Workspace status mutation — the defect is the absence of a §23.4-specific schema, not an absence of all audit logging. P1 is correct.
- D-23-007 — held at **P1**: §23.1 actively contradicts §4.4.1's field set (not merely silent on it).
- D-23-008 — held at **P1**: `bid_owner_id` "single owner" wording would forbid Bid Contributors and contradicts §23.2's two-user lock model.
- D-23-011 — held at **P1**: no error path is buildable.
- D-23-016 — held at **P1**: 5 s vs 30 s contradiction is not "ambiguity a thoughtful engineer can resolve" — it is a hard conflict with §25.2.1's normative SLO.
- D-23-018 — held at **P2**: the prose ambiguity ("in a transaction" vs "partial success") is reader-resolvable to "best-effort with per-row settlement" by reading §32.6.1; P2 not P1.
- D-23-012 — held at **P2**: numerical singletons rule is well-established but inline literals are mechanically resolvable (move to §39).
- D-23-022 / D-23-024 / D-23-025 / D-23-026 / D-23-027 — held at **P2** (silence on applicable dimensions where the conventional resolution exists in §40.2 / §38 / §37 / §42 / §44; engineering would build it consistently).
- D-23-023 — held at **P2**: firewall *leakage* is a high-stakes class but the specific defect is that the *test* of firewall integrity is not asserted in §23 ACs (the underlying §1.3 / §25.1.2 rules are intact). Not a P0 because no actual leak is present in the implementation as currently spec'd.
- D-23-028 — held at **P2**: idempotency gap is reader-resolvable from §32.8.0 but with material implementation impact.
- D-23-029 — held at **P2**: reversal asymmetry is a product question with both authoring paths viable.
- D-23-030 / D-23-031 — held at **P3** (cosmetic; do not block implementation).

No defect downgraded to evade rule (4) of the Severity rule. No defect upgraded above the rule warrants. Two defect candidates were considered and rejected:
- §23.2 "advisory lock" terminology vs Convex compare-and-swap mechanism — internally consistent if `response.lock` is treated as an application-level field. Filing as D-23-009 (schema absence) covered the implementation gap; no separate semantic defect needed.
- §23.5 "Withdrawal confirmation modal prevents accidental withdrawal" — toothless AC (does not specify what "prevents" means). Already covered under D-23-017 (AC fidelity).

### Phase 24 Counterfactual Pass

For each §24 surface audited, three realistic failure modes were enumerated and the spec was checked against each. Promoted to defects:

- **Seller Q&A.** (1) NDA expires mid-Phase-7 — Q&A read-access behavior silent (D-24-002). (2) Vendor reaches §18.2.3 50-question cap on multi-team seller-side bid — aggregation semantics silent (D-24-004). (3) Buyer toggles thread visibility; cached seller-side projections via the bridge — silent (folded into D-24-002).
- **NDA Module.** (1) Buyer uploads NDA v2 mid-vendor-signing v1 — race resolution silent (D-24-015 + D-24-018). (2) Buyer revokes NDA — no `revoke` action; only `expired` time-based state (D-24-016 + D-24-019). (3) Signing user later DSAR-erased — `nda_buyer_signatory_email` / `nda_seller_signatory_email` PII; no DSAR clause (D-24-028).
- **Seller Inbox.** (1) Buyer pushes 200 amendment re-verification requests — rate-limit / aggregation silent (D-24-005 + D-24-006). (2) Inbox item from canceled Bid Workspace — cleanup cascade silent (folded into D-24-005). (3) Loops.so outage during fan-out — §24.3-specific fallback silent (D-24-008).
- **Seller Pulse.** (1) Concurrent submission storm causes "real-time" lag — no SLO, no degradation (D-24-011). (2) `seller_solo` plan with `evaluation_owner_mode=solo` — surface-suppression silent (D-24-014). (3) Bid Workspace `disqualified` — final Pulse value freeze silent (D-24-012).
- **Seller Analytics.** (1) No submitted bids in last quarter — empty state silent (D-24-032). (2) Multi-Org seller per-Org partition — silent (folded into D-24-022). (3) Analytics export under DSAR-pending state — partial-data export contract silent (folded into D-24-029).

## Phase 5 — Prompt 5.6 — §26 Seller Profiles, Verification & Capability Declarations Walk (2026-05-06)

**Scope.** Walk Master Spec §26 (lines 21116–21830) end-to-end. Confirm the five prompt-mandated checks: (a) public seller profile schema cites SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage in §4.4; (b) verification tiers (Basic / Verified / Certified) match §34.16 Marketplace Discovery Pricing; (c) VerificationReviewRecord lifecycle is fully spec'd; (d) capability declarations cite Capability Registry in §21.4; (e) vendor opt-out cascade (§4.5 / §4.7) is honored. Apply the V0 14-check audit checklist on top. Walk every adjacent surface (§4.4.3 Seller Profile, §4.4.4 Capability Declaration, §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record, §4.4.9 SellerSoftware, §4.4.10 SellerOrgPage, §4.4.11 SoftwarePage, §4.4.21 VerificationReviewRecord, §4.5.6 Vendor Opt-Out Marketplace-Domain Read & Render Contract, §21.4 Capability Registry, §22.14.3 KB-to-Capability evidence-overlap rule, §27.4 Match Score, §29102 Entitlement Matrix, §29616 plan-tier gates, §34.16 Marketplace Discovery Pricing, Appendix B Keyboard Shortcuts, Appendix C Notification Events, Appendix I Error Codes, Appendix J Controlled Vocabulary, Appendix K Glossary, Appendix L State Machines, Appendix M.1 Surface/Engine Mapping). Findings scratch log at `_audit/PHASE5.6_FINDINGS.md`.

**Verdict.** Three of five prompt-mandated checks FAIL outright. Public profile schema (Check 1) does NOT cite §4.4.3 from §26.1, and §26.1 names a `verification_tier` Seller Profile field that does not exist in §4.4.3. Verification tier criteria (Check 2) are mutually inconsistent across §26.2 / §4.4.21 / §34.16.2 — three different definitions for Basic / Verified / Certified that a junior engineer would build differently depending on which source they read first. Capability declarations (Check 4) do NOT cite §21.4 Capability Registry from §26.3 or §26.4; §26.3 carries a v6.0.0 thin schema (6 fields, 3-state verification status) that contradicts the v7.0.0 §4.4.4 schema (25 fields, 7-state lifecycle). Verification lifecycle (Check 3) is fully authored in §4.4.21 but not surfaced from §26.2. Opt-out cascade (Check 5) is honored at the page level but conflicts with §4.5.6 on the HTTP response code (200 vs 410), and is silent on capability-declaration redaction. 25 defects filed below — 1 P0, 8 P1, 12 P2, 4 P3.

**Self-challenge withdrawals.** None. All findings survived the hostile-reviewer pass; severity classifications hold (P0 for the billing-mode contradiction; P1 for buildability gaps; P2 for ambiguity-not-blocking; P3 for cosmetic drift). Two findings consolidated to avoid duplication: §26.7.2 enrichment retry curve (originally separate) folded into D-5.6-011 numerical-singleton cluster; §26.4 confidence threshold under-cite folded into D-5.6-010.

- **F-415 Seller Profile:** verification-tier-not-yet-earned (covered, default `basic` per §27.4.3); profile delete during pending VerificationReviewRecord (silent, deferred to F-416); marketplace_opted_in flip mid-evaluation (partially covered, §4.4.10 state machine).

- **F-417 Capability Declarations:** cross-org evidence (covered, §4.4.4 invariant #3); narrative-only with capability prose (covered, §4.4.4 AC #8 nudge); deprecated-category quarantine (covered, §4.4.4 state machine).
- **F-419 Seller Organization Page:** domain verification revoked post-publication (covered, §26.7.3); concurrent enrichment requests (covered, §26.7.2 7-day rate limit); enrichment service down (covered, §26.7.2 failure modes table).
- **F-420 SellerOrgPage Enrichment:** **billing-mode contradiction (UNRESOLVED — D-5.6-001 P0)**; anti-spam rejection (covered, §26.7.2); Firecrawl partial-crawl (silent — under-specified).
- **F-423 SellerSoftware & Software Pages:** concurrent claim attempts (covered, §26.8.2 dispute resolution); transfer mid-bid (covered, §26.8.7); soft-delete cascade (covered, §26.8.1 + §4.4.11).
- **Vendor opt-out cascade:** opt-out during in-flight enrichment AIOperation (silent — D-5.6-023 covers); opt-out during claim dispute (silent); cached-page race (covered, §26.7.6 60-second snapshot TTL).

## Phase 5 — Prompt 5.7 — §49 Seller Onboarding Implementation-Level Seven-Stage Flow Walk (2026-05-06)

**Scope.** Walk Master Spec §49 (lines 37176–37708) end-to-end. Confirm the eight prompt-mandated checks: (1) all seven stages defined with entry/exit conditions; (2) magic-link → first-requirement-response p50 < 20 min activation metric is testable, citing §51; (3) Forced-Vendor-Signup playbook (Summary C.136; prompt-side miscited as C.137) reflected; (4) Hero Moment mechanics (Summary §3.6) reflected; (5) Three Conversion Moments (Summary C.133; prompt-side miscited as C.135) reflected; (6) Onboarding anti-patterns (Summary C.141; prompt-side miscited as C.140) flagged forbidden; (7) plan-gating differentiates Free / Solo / paid onboarding paths; (8) drop-off recovery spec'd via §41 + §20. Apply the V0 14-check audit checklist on top. Walk every adjacent surface (§4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession entity, §48.1.7 Three Conversion Moments binding, §48.8.3 / §48.8.4 / §48.8.5 / §48.8.6 / §48.8.7 / §48.8.10 Hero Moment + AP authoring, §51.1.1 / §51.1.2 / §51.1.5 / §51.2.1 telemetry envelope, §41.2 email catalog, §20 Inbox, §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment, §34.1.2 / §34.2.5 / §34.10.4 plan tiers, §21.4 Capability Registry, Appendix J `seller_onboarding_completion_state` / `seller_onboarding_invite_source` / `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_kind` / `onboarding_anti_pattern_kind` enums, Appendix C Notification Events, Appendix I Error Codes, Appendix M.1 surface mapping). Findings scratch log at `_audit/PHASE5.7_FINDINGS.md`.

**Verdict.** Five of eight prompt-mandated checks FAIL. Stage 6 has no atomic exit timestamp (Check 1). Activation Metric ACs do not cite §51 envelope/family conformance (Check 2). Three Conversion Moments are not all reflected and §49.1.7 conflates a fourth construct (`loss_debrief_insight_gate`) into the §48.1.7 enum (Check 5). Plan-gating is silent on Solo (Check 7). Drop-off recovery is silent across all stages, §41.2 has zero seller-onboarding re-engagement templates, and §20 inbox nudges are not referenced (Check 8). On top of the prompt-scoped checks, §49 vs §4.4.22 schema/contract drift is pervasive: `completion_state='churned_post_activation'` is unregistered (D-5.7-001); §49.1.1 fail-mode-6 contradicts §4.4.22 reactivation invariant (D-5.7-002); abandonment threshold drift across 7d/14d/60d (D-5.7-003); four `stage_7_*` AE columns referenced but not in §4.4.22 (D-5.7-004); `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents` referenced but not in §4.4.22 (D-5.7-005); §49.1.1 invite_source enum incomplete (D-5.7-007). Stage 3 mid-streaming abandonment burns lifetime-free allowance with no compensation contract (D-5.7-024). 24 defects filed below — 0 P0, 14 P1, 7 P2, 3 P3. (D-5.7-015 and D-5.7-016 are promoted to P1 per the audit-prompt OUTPUT clause's explicit P1 trigger for "any of the seven stages with a silent edge case (timeout, abandon, third-party outage)" — overrides the standard Severity Definitions for §49 audit scope.)

**Self-challenge withdrawals.** None. All findings survived the hostile-reviewer pass; severity classifications hold. One finding (D-5.7-024 Stage-3 mid-streaming abandonment) was added during the self-challenge pass after re-reading §49.1.3 step 3 with the failure-mode lens — the lifetime-free allowance is a one-shot grant and abandoning mid-stream burns it permanently, satisfying the audit prompt's P1 trigger for "any of the seven stages with a silent edge case (timeout, abandon, third-party outage)."

**Audit-prompt source-citation errata (advisory; not a spec defect).** The Phase-5.7 prompt body at `Audit_Prompts.md` lines 1599–1610 contains three Summary C-citation errors: "C.137" should be C.136 (Forced-Vendor-Signup); "C.135" should be C.133 (Three Conversion Moments); "C.140" should be C.141 (Onboarding Anti-Patterns). Master Spec §49 uses the canonical numbering throughout and is correct.

### Phase 5.7 Counterfactual Pass

For each of the seven stages, three realistic failure modes were enumerated and tested for spec coverage. Per the audit prompt, P1 was filed for any stage with a silent edge case (timeout, abandon, third-party outage):

- **Stage 1 Magic-Link Arrival.** Timeout: render p95 ≤ 500ms covered (AC 1). Abandon: 14-day staleness sweep covered but no re-engagement → D-5.7-008. Third-party: WorkOS covered, Loops.so outage for magic-link-fallback not covered → subsumed under D-5.7-008 / D-5.7-016.
- **Stage 2 Domain Bootstrap.** Timeout: 10,000ms p90 alerting covered (AC 8) but no hard circuit-breaker; Bootstrap exceeds latency target → degraded UI covered. Abandon: Bootstrap continues server-side without seller awareness; not covered. Third-party: Firecrawl ✅, Anthropic Opus ✅, WorkOS ✅, Convex ❌ → D-5.7-015, PostHog ❌ → D-5.7-015.
- **Stage 3 First-Pass Draft.** Timeout: 90s batch budget covered (AC 17). Abandon: mid-streaming session close burns lifetime-free allowance with no compensation contract → D-5.7-024 (P1). Third-party: Sonnet covered.
- **Stage 4 Landing Screen.** Timeout: paint > 500ms tracked (AC 25). Abandon: counter dismiss + browser back covered; never-engage-then-leave → no re-engagement, subsumed under D-5.7-008. Third-party: paint-only stage; PostHog meta-event would not block.
- **Stage 5 In-Workspace Review.** Timeout: per-AIOperation timeout deferred to §48.8.4 / §34.6 settlement contract. Abandon: §49.1.5 fm 8 covers "completes all requirements but never submits" with 14d sweep and no re-engagement → subsumed under D-5.7-008. Third-party: Anthropic outage during edit → partial degradation noted but not explicit.
- **Stage 6 First Bid Submission.** Timeout: Stake-Reveal computation timeout not specified (default to §44.x perf budget). Abandon: §49.1.6 fm 3 covers "closes tab before paint." Third-party: kb_to_capability_suggestion / page_enrichment outages covered. **Stage 6 EXIT is implicit — no atomic timestamp** → D-5.7-010 (P1).
- **Stage 7 Post-Submission Debrief.** Timeout: bid-resolution wait could be infinite; §10.14 phase-timeout sweep partially addresses. Abandon: 60-day post-activation staleness → `churned_post_activation` (unregistered enum, D-5.7-001) + no re-engagement (D-5.7-008). Third-party: win_loss_insight_synthesis covered, Loops.so for debrief notification → D-5.7-016, Anthropic outage → partial coverage.

## Phase 6 — Prompt 6.1 — Cross-Console Mechanics (§25 + §4.7) End-to-End Audit (2026-05-06)

**Scope.** Walk §25 end-to-end (§25.1 through §25.7) with cross-reference to §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event and §4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification Record. Cross-check §1.3 Dual-Console Data Isolation, §1.4 Query Scoping, §6.8 DSAR, §31 Webhooks, §32.8 idempotency, §40.2 Retention, §42 Observability, §51 PostHog envelope, §50 Ops Console kill-switch, Appendix C / F / G / I / J / K / L / M. Findings scratch log at `_audit/PHASE6.1_FINDINGS.md` (audit posture: non-destructive — no Master Spec edits performed in this prompt; v7.1.0 unchanged).

**Verdict.** Six of seven prompt-mandated checks FAIL; one (CHECK #4 Replay/Idempotency) passes. CHECK #6 Console Firewall Integrity carries one P0 (`fanout_group_id` cardinality side-channel — single-seller exposure leaks competing-vendor count). 23 defects filed: 1 P0, 12 P1, 7 P2, 3 P3. Per the prompt's halt rule (P0 firewall defects halt the audit), Phase 6.1 is HALTED pending D-6.1-001 remediation; Phase 6.2 (§27 Marketplace) MUST NOT advance until D-6.1-001 is resolved or formally downgraded with Counsel + Security sign-off.

**Self-challenge withdrawals.** Two candidate findings withdrawn: (a) `superseded_by_event_id` cross-fanout-group inference — folded into D-6.1-001 because the failure mode is the same fan-out cardinality leak; (b) `firewall_isolation_token` opacity — withdrawn as already-pseudonymous and not a leak vector.

FX-locking (§4.8.1 AC #5 + Failure Mode #5) found internally consistent for AIOperations; the Solo-per-charge FX-lock-time gap was filed earlier as D-PT-005 and is not re-filed.

### Phase CONS Self-Challenge Pass

- D-CONS-001 self-challenge: "Could a thoughtful staff engineer reconcile §34.3.3 row vs §4.8.6 AC #2 by treating the row as a 'hard' block and AC #2 as a 'soft' approval?" Reviewed — no. The §4.8.6 AC #2 explicitly says "MUST require explicit `ops_finance_admin` approval before publication" — that's a publish-blocker. The §34.3.3 row "auto-publish block | ≥ 25%" is also a publish-blocker. They contradict on threshold value, not on enforcement strength. P0 stands.
- D-CONS-002 self-challenge: "Could AC #3's 'all writes' be read as 'all NORMAL writes' with the state-machine row as the implicit Ops carve-out?" The Settlement Freeze block at line 8168 explicitly enumerates: "only `redacted_at` (DSAR) writes are accepted. All other writes return `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement` (HTTP 422)." That's exhaustive enumeration; no implicit carve-out. P0 stands.
- D-CONS-009 self-challenge: "Could the FreeAllowanceCounter / plan-tier reconciliation be inferred from the §34.10.3 burn priority?" Reviewed — no. Burn priority establishes ORDER (free → commit → included → overage), but does not establish whether free-allowance and plan-tier-entitlement counters are the SAME counter or SEPARATE counters. P1 stands.
- D-CONS-010 self-challenge: "Is the Solo envelope counter implicit in `AIOperation` rows (`console=buyer` / `console=seller` filtered sum)?" Theoretically yes — engineering could compute consumed Solo envelope from AIOperation aggregation. But that's not a counter; that's a derived metric. The §34.10.3 throttling logic + §44.6.4 throttling threshold need an O(1) counter read, not a sum. P1 stands.
- D-CONS-014 severity revision: Initially considered P1 (cross-reference integrity) but lowered to P2 — engineering CAN find the AIOperation state machine inline in §4.8.1 by following the cross-references, just less efficient. P2 stands.

**Phase EM Self-Challenge Pass (Opus-mandatory).** Re-read the 20 defects above as a hostile reviewer.

- **D-EM-001 / D-EM-014.** Reproducible: `qa_suggestion_buyer` and `kb_suggestion` cross-console example are explicit references to non-existent matrix instances. Severity P0 holds for D-EM-001 (deploy-time validator failure); P1 for D-EM-014 (narrative example, lower runtime risk).
- **D-EM-002 / D-EM-003 / D-EM-004 / D-EM-007 / D-EM-008.** All flagged capabilities produce a null `ctx.db.capabilityRegistryEntry(capabilityId)` lookup at the §34.8.2 runtime path. The runtime code as written will throw on `cap.enforcement_mode` access; this is a P0 build blocker even before the matrix-completeness validator runs. Confirmed P0 except D-EM-007 (P1; mixed AI + non-AI rows; AI portion is the only true P0 — `proactive_marketplace_eoi`) and D-EM-008 (P3; AE-pending — runtime impact only after AE signoff lands).
- **D-EM-005 / D-EM-006 / D-EM-009 / D-EM-017 / D-EM-018.** All instances of one structural defect: §34.8.5 has been used as a catch-all gating registry rather than the AI-capability runtime contract its preamble defines. Considered consolidating into one super-defect, kept separate so each can be tracked / fixed / regressed independently. The recommended dispositions form a coherent program: scope the matrix to AI capabilities only; relocate non-AI gating to §5.11. Severity P1 / P2 — runtime path for non-AI gating already exists at the API/RBAC layer; matrix entries are stale documentation, not load-bearing runtime contracts.
- **D-EM-010 / D-EM-011 / D-EM-012.** Column-typing defects. Severity P1 / P2 — degrade automation but do not block runtime evaluation today.
- **D-EM-013 / D-EM-014.** Cross-document drift. Severity P1 because Authoring Convention #10 is breached but the runtime path consumes only the matrix.
- **D-EM-015.** Validator-naming hygiene. P2; QA can write the test once the name is stable.
- **D-EM-016 / D-EM-019 / D-EM-020.** Engine-side completeness gaps that engineers will paper over with judgment calls. Each will produce divergent implementations.

No defect was downgraded on review. D-EM-005 and D-EM-006 considered for consolidation but kept distinct (different remediation owners, different phase impact).

**Phase EM Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass (Opus-mandatory).**

For the §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix surface, three realistic failure modes the spec must handle:

1. **A new customer-billed capability is added to §21.4 but the §34.8.5 matrix row is forgotten.** Spec coverage: §34.8.7 acceptance criterion #6 declares a deploy-time validator. Validator unnamed (D-EM-015). Resolution lands in D-EM-002 / D-EM-015 fixes.
2. **A `low_priority_background` Solo capability exhausts envelope; toast fires; capability not in matrix; entitlement check has no plan-gate to honor.** Spec coverage: §44.6.4.1 names the three capabilities; matrix has no rows; runtime resolution undefined. Defect filed: D-EM-004. Recommendation: matrix row + registry seed + Solo envelope flag.
3. **An AE row is invoked before signoff lands.** Spec coverage: §34.8.5 AE activation lock paragraph (line 29278) says return `capability_not_signed_off` (HTTP 422); error code presence in Appendix I unverified (defer to Phase 12). After AE signoff, registry row still missing → null runtime lookup → throw. Defect filed: D-EM-008. Recommendation: confirm Appendix I row; require both AE signoff AND registry row before activation.

A fourth failure mode worth recording (not yet a defect because spec arguably handles it): **Plan-tier downgrade mid-billing-period invalidates a soft-gated capability that's mid-invocation.** §34.8.6 #1 covers this for `pending` operations under the prior wallet rules. Edge case is explicitly handled.

**Promotion to DEFECT_LEDGER.md.** 20 defects promoted (D-EM-001 through D-EM-020).

## Phase MD — §34.16 Marketplace Discovery Pricing (Non-AI Layer) Walk (2026-05-07)

### Phase MD Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read the 20 defects above as a hostile reviewer. Each defect was stress-tested for reproducibility, severity rule-fit, and recommendation sharpness; revisions logged in `PHASE34.16_FINDINGS.md` §3. No findings revised on review. D-MD-005 considered for downgrade to P2 on the rationalization that Vickrey auction transparency may justify winner-identity disclosure — rejected because the spec does not articulate that rationalization and the §34.16.1 *Anonymization* block + §27.11.1 design principle 4 set the contrary expectation. D-MD-001 considered for downgrade to P3 on substantive grounds (Solo plans don't transact §34.16 SKUs anyway) — rejected because CLAUDE.md §16 Phase 14.9.2 inline-plan-tier audit catalogues 5-tier inline restatements as P1.

### Phase MD Counterfactual Pass

Three realistic failure modes per SKU evaluated in `PHASE34.16_FINDINGS.md` §4. Two unhandled cases promoted to defects: D-MD-014 (cascade pricing on insolvency) and D-MD-016 (cross-marketplace-domain leakage). One additional case (mid-period revocation of paid-mode Featured Placement) determined to be sufficiently covered by §27.11.4 cancellation row.

## Phase 9 — Prompt 9.1 — Retention Per Data Class (§40.2) End-to-End Walk (2026-05-08)

The §40.2 retention walk per `Audit_Prompts.md` lines 2108–2133 (Prompt 9.1: "Retention Per Data Class — §40.2"). Twenty-two unique defects filed: **8 P0 / 12 P1 / 1 P2 / 1 — (consolidated)**. All five required CHECKS in the prompt FAIL; reverse-pass against §4 finds 50 of 75 entities (~67%) absent from §40.2. Halt rule "zero P0 in retention/DSAR surface" — **FAIL** (8 P0). Advancement to Prompt 9.2 (DSAR Compatibility) **HALTED** until the P0 cluster is remediated.

**ID-mnemonic note.** Per `Audit_Prompts.md` Defect Ledger Format line 55, mnemonic IDs are permitted "to keep prompt-scoped ID strings stable across rolls of the phase numbering". The prior 2026-05-08 ledger entry under "Phase 9 — Prompt 9.1" (lines 3186–3231) was an Appendix G PostHog walk mislabeled as 9.1 (it is structurally Prompt 8.4 per Audit_Prompts.md line 2007), and consumed `D-9.1-001`..`D-9.1-021`. To preserve immutability of those IDs and disambiguate the two runs, this run uses the mnemonic form `D-9.1R-NNN` (R = Retention). Mapping to scratch log: `D-9.1R-NNN` here ↔ `D-9.1-NNN` in `PHASE9_FINDINGS.md`. The mislabeling itself is queued as a P3 documentation defect for the next V phase.

**Cluster pattern.** The §40.2 contract is structurally inverted: entity sections (§4.6.1.1, §4.6.2, §4.6.5, §4.7.1.1, §4.8.1, §4.8.3, §4.2.5, §22.4.1) currently OWN retention rules and §40.2 is a partial mirror. CLAUDE.md §11 / Master Spec §10 require the inverse — §40.2 as canonical singleton, entity sections cite. The single largest fix is restoring §40.2 to canonical posture (D-9.1R-022) and authoring rows for the 50 absent entities (rolled into D-9.1R-009..-017).

## Phase SS — UI Surface State Coverage Audit (2026-05-10)

**Sweep scope.** Every `feature_class = surface` row in `_audit/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md` (≈95 rows). For each surface, the eight required state dimensions (loading / empty / error / retry / partial-completion / permission-denied / plan-gated upgrade-CTA / Solo Mode suppression) walked end-to-end against the Master Spec. **P1 filed for any surface missing more than two required states**, per the Phase SS task brief.

**Methodology.** §3.7 (Loading / Empty / Error State Catalog) defines six page-type taxonomies (`dashboard`, `matrix`, `detail`, `settings`, `ops_console`, `knowledge_base`). The §3.7.6.x catalog applies *implicitly* to any surface mapping to one of those classes, but per-surface inheritance must be explicit (per the Audit-Prompts edge-case discipline). Surfaces that do not bind to §3.7.6.x or do not name `page_surface_kind` are treated as silent on the inherited state. Solo Mode disposition per §44.6.1.

**Severity rule.** P1 = surface unbuildable as written (junior engineer would build divergent partial-completion / retry / Solo treatment); the rule is the standard ledger §1 P1 rule. No P0 surfaced (no firewall / regulatory / billing-leakage class triggered).

## Phase 37 — §37 Accessibility & Internationalization End-to-End Audit (2026-05-10)

**Sweep scope.** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` §37 (lines 31357–31398) walked end-to-end against the prompt's 8 named CHECKS plus the Master Spec authoring conventions. Cross-referenced §3.6 (forms a11y), §3.8 (Peek focus trap), §3.9.7 (cursor presence a11y), §3.10 (bulk action a11y), §3.11 (dark mode contrast gate + High Contrast Mode), §3.12 (presence/unread a11y), §30.6 (palette keyboard a11y), §36.1 (User Settings — no Accessibility panel), §38.6 (per-tier touch targets), §38.10 (reduced-motion pointer), §38.11 (RTL `useDirectionality()` hook authored — directly contradicts §37.3 deferral), Appendix B §B.10 (Accessibility Notes), Appendix M.1 (no §37 engine rows).

**Methodology.** Walked the audit-prompt 14-point checklist on §37 plus the four in-scope features (F-569 WCAG 2.1 AA Contract / F-570 i18n Architecture / F-571 RTL Support / F-572 Accessibility Testing Pipeline) plus the secondary anchor F-065 High Contrast Mode. WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criteria 1.3.5 (Input Purpose), 1.4.10 (Reflow), 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast), 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable), 2.2.2 (Pause/Stop/Hide), 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), 2.5.5 (Target Size), 3.1.1 (Language of Page), 3.1.2 (Language of Parts) used as the conformance reference set.

**Severity rule.** Per the prompt's OUTPUT directive: "accessibility gaps are P1 minimum if they affect WCAG AA conformance." Section-level aggregation gaps that two engineers would resolve differently (without breaching WCAG AA) held at P2. Cosmetic / stale-version-label drift at P3. No P0 surfaced (no firewall / regulatory / billing-leakage class triggered).

**Defect-ID convention.** `D-37-NNN`, sequential within phase. Mnemonic-bound per `Audit_Prompts.md → Defect Ledger Format`.

**Full scratch log.** `_audit/PHASE37_FINDINGS.md` (counterfactual pass, self-challenge pass, severity roll-up, halt-rule evaluation, AE-ledger forward references).

## Phase 38 — §38 Responsive Design & Platform Support End-to-End Audit (2026-05-11)

**Sweep scope.** `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` §38 (lines 31402–31938) walked end-to-end against the prompt's six named CHECKS plus the Master Spec authoring conventions. Cross-referenced §3.4 Mobile Translation of Linear Constraint (lines 2285–2306), §3 line 3433 (iOS/Android app-backgrounded Convex subscription pause), §29.3 push-notification user preferences, §44.1 Performance Targets (lines 32701–32722), §50.14.3 Growth PM Dashboard (lines 40302–40316), §50.14.4 GTM Lead Dashboard (lines 40318–40330), Appendix C Notification Event Catalog, Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy preamble + standard / advanced / billing tables, Appendix I API Error Code Catalog, Appendix J Controlled Vocabulary Registry, Appendix K Glossary, Appendix M.1 Master Surface/Engine Mapping Table, Appendix M.5 CI Gate Catalog (95 gates), §6.8.4.3 DSAR Cascade Class Coverage Registry (V9 gate `dsar_cascade_class_coverage_completeness`), §40.2 Retention Per Data Class (V9 gate `entity_retention_coverage_on_diff`), §1.3 / §7.2 Buyer/Seller Console Firewall, and §38.6.5 / §38.8.5 release-gate references.

**Methodology.** Walked the audit-prompt 14-point checklist against the §38 in-scope features per `_audit/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md` (F-573 through F-590 plus secondary anchors F-027, F-040, F-042, F-051, F-054, F-067, F-571, F-634, F-AE-006). The prompt's six named CHECKS each mapped to one or more defects: (1) Breakpoints — D-38-007; (2) §3.4 reflection — D-38-027 + secondary noise; (3) Per-surface mobile parity — D-38-010; (4) Native-app surface — D-38-025; (5) Touch-target sizes — D-38-008 (consolidate with Phase-37 D-37-001); (6) Performance budgets — D-38-009.

**Severity rule.** Per Severity Definitions block above (rule-based; first matching rule wins). Mobile-divergence and accessibility gaps held at P2 unless they affect WCAG AA conformance, leave a feature unbuildable, or break a CI gate referenced as merge-blocking.

**Defect-ID convention.** `D-38-NNN`, sequential within phase. Mnemonic-bound per `Audit_Prompts.md → Defect Ledger Format`.

## Phase 42 — §42 Observability, Reliability & Disaster Recovery End-to-End Audit (2026-05-11)

Audit prompt: Walk Master Spec §42 end-to-end. Eight checks: (1) per-service SLOs; (2) structured logging schema + PII scrubbing; (3) every revenue-affecting event has a metric; (4) distributed tracing across MCP / Managed Agents / Stripe / WorkOS; (5) every SLO violation pages; (6) every alert links to a runbook; (7) RTO/RPO per service; (8) DR drills cadence. ### Phase 43 Halt-Rule Evaluation

P0 = 6 found (D-43-001, D-43-002, D-43-003, D-43-004, D-43-005, D-43-006). Per `Audit_Prompts.md` Global Verification Protocol, an unresolved P0 halts forward progress. **Phase 43 halts at audit closure pending remediation of all six P0 defects.** Recommended remediation sequence:

1. **D-43-018 (P1) closure FIRST** as the root-cause meta-fix. Adding a retirement banner at §43 head with a "MUST follow §50" pointer immediately demotes the operational risk of all six P0 defects from "junior engineer builds the wrong thing" to "junior engineer reads the banner first." This is a single-paragraph spec edit and is the highest-leverage move.
2. **D-43-001 / D-43-007 closure pack.** Retire §43.2 in place; add the `is_staff_legacy_gate_forbidden` CI gate.
3. **D-43-002 / D-43-013 closure pack.** Either (a) retire §43.1 capability list to a §50 pointer, or (b) extend Appendix J `ops_capability_kind` with the 14 missing values and bind matrix rows in §50.3.2; either path also closes D-43-013 state-machine gap (state machines move to home sections).
4. **D-43-003 / D-43-006 closure pack.** Retire §43.3 "Assume user session" + "Workspace Export" lines; route to §50.4 + §50.2.3 contract surfaces.
5. **D-43-004 / D-43-009 closure pack.** Retire §43.4 admin_audit_log table; route to §4.6.1 Audit Event + §50.5 Ops-Tagged Audit Actor.
6. **D-43-005 closure.** Retire §43.1 GDPR-data-export line to §6.8 pointer.
7. **D-43-008 closure.** Retire §43.5 ACs to §50.8 aggregate AC pointer.
8. **P1 long-tail.** D-43-010 / D-43-011 / D-43-012 / D-43-014 / D-43-015 / D-43-016 / D-43-017 either resolve naturally if §43 is fully retired (preferred) or each requires a dedicated remediation pack.
9. **P2 / P3 cleanup.** D-43-019 (mobile-divergence declaration); D-43-020 (broken §43.4.2 citation at line 49644); D-43-021 (anchor slug `&` / escaped-dot normalization).

The lowest-touch path forward is a single Master Spec edit that (a) adds the D-43-018 banner at §43 head, (b) retires §43.1 / §43.2 / §43.3 / §43.4 / §43.5 prose to one-line pointers into §50, (c) updates the Appendix M.1 §43-block to reflect retirement, (d) drops the inline `admin_audit_log` schema and `is_staff` references, (e) wires three new CI gates (`is_staff_legacy_gate_forbidden`, `admin_audit_log_table_forbidden`, `legacy_assume_user_session_button_forbidden`) into §M.5. This closes 14 of 21 defects (D-43-001 through -013 and -018) in a single coordinated edit; the remaining P1s (D-43-010 / -011 / -012 / -014 / -015 / -016 / -017) and P2 / P3 cleanup land in the same Phase 43 remediation pack.

### Phase 43 Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read 21 findings as a hostile reviewer:

- **D-43-001** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "is_staff is just a legacy boolean; §50 governs in practice." Rebuttal: §43.2 prose remains in-place with no retirement banner. A junior engineer following the v6.0.0-era authoring discipline (read §N before §N+1) reaches §43.2 first and implements the boolean; the §50.3 matrix is bypassed. P0 rule (b) PII / capability scope exposure stands. Considered demotion to P1; rejected because the harm chain is concrete (impersonation + refund + plan override + DSAR initiation all gated on one bit).
- **D-43-002** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "the §50 preamble says §50 prevails; the CI gate `ops_capability_matrix_coverage_complete` would fail in CI before reaching prod." Rebuttal: §M.5 catalog at v7.1.0 shows 119 gates as `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` per CLAUDE.md §16 — `ops_capability_matrix_coverage_complete` is in that pending set, not runtime-active. Per P0 rule (e), CI gate runtime-unwireable applies; P0 stands.
- **D-43-003** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "Enterprise support only is sufficient gating." Rebuttal: tier-scope is a customer-facing classification, not an Ops role / capability gate; an Enterprise-tier customer's Org can still have its session assumed by any `is_staff` user without quorum, justification, or time-box. P0 rule (a) + (b) + (c) stands.
- **D-43-004** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "parallel table doesn't break integrity if reads are unified." Rebuttal: §5.2.1.4 Billing Admin Audit View reads §4.6.1 by anchor — if admin_audit_log is the destination, customer Org Owners never see the Ops attribution chip. P0 rule (c) audit-log integrity stands.
- **D-43-005** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "GDPR is regulatory; engineering wouldn't ship an unverified DSAR." Rebuttal: §43.1 is the engineering build spec and it does not cite §6.8.6.1 verification; the rule is "build what the spec says." P0 rule (c) regulatory stands.
- **D-43-006** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "Workspace Export is a one-line note." Rebuttal: a one-line note in a build spec is a feature directive; the absence of residency / firewall / redaction qualifications is the defect. P0 rule (a) + (b) + (c) stands.
- **D-43-007** held at **P1**. Considered P0 (rbac unbuildable); rejected because the missing field schema is a buildability defect rather than a runtime exposure (the runtime exposure is captured by D-43-001). P1 stands.
- **D-43-008** held at **P1**. Considered P0 (AC #4 directly contradicts §50.2.3 in a way that could trigger compliance audits). Rejected because AC contradictions are caught by code review against §50 in practice. P1 stands.
- **D-43-009 / D-43-010 / D-43-011 / D-43-012 / D-43-013 / D-43-014 / D-43-015 / D-43-016 / D-43-017** held at **P1** per Defect Ledger Format P1 rule: feature unbuildable as written (missing retention / error codes / API contracts / webhook contracts / state machines / surface row / firewall declaration / residency clause / posthog events).
- **D-43-018** held at **P1**. Considered P0 root-cause (every P0 above stems from the absent retirement banner). Rejected because the retirement banner itself is a documentation fix, not a runtime invariant — the runtime risks are properly attributed to the downstream P0 defects. P1 stands.
- **D-43-019** held at **P2** (mobile parity not specified — ambiguity resolvable but not consistent across readers).
- **D-43-020 / D-43-021** held at **P3** (broken citation; anchor-slug hygiene).

No defects demoted from P0.

### Phase 50 Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read 40 findings as a hostile reviewer:

- **D-50-006** held at **P0**. Reviewer challenge: "Plan override is a sales-ops manual process, not a programmatic surface; engineering wouldn't ship a code path for it." Rebuttal: §43.1 line 32651 enumerates it as an Admin Dashboard capability; §26107 references "Sales-Ops manual provisioning" without authoring the path. Without an authored surface, the path is implemented ad-hoc (Stripe metadata edit, Convex direct mutation under break-glass, etc.) — all of which bypass the §50.2.4 no-direct-DB-access rule. P0 rule (d) revenue-leakage stands; P0 rule (e) `ops_capability_matrix_coverage_complete` CI gate is runtime-unwireable without registration. Considered demotion to P1; rejected because the absence of any authored constraint makes the surface materially worse than a constrained-but-imperfect surface.
- **D-50-002 / D-50-032** held at **P1**. Reviewer challenge: "These are pedantic contradictions; engineering picks one and moves on." Rebuttal: the field is declared NOT NULL in §50.12 / §50.13 entity tables; the field "must not exist" per §4.6.3 authoring intent. Engineering would either silently null the field (breaking the NOT NULL constraint) or invent a synthetic OpsSession (departing from §4.6.3 intent). Both produce drift. P1 stands.
- **D-50-003** held at **P1**. Considered demotion to P2 because §26.7 + §24910 does declare an Ops surface for verification review. Rejected because §26.7 is feature-area authoring without §50-fidelity coverage of UX screen inventory / Ops-only API / capability envelope rows / Appendix C-G-I-J registrations. A junior engineer building from §26 would not produce the same surface as §50.11 Template Review. P1 stands.
- **D-50-005 / D-50-008 / D-50-009 / D-50-010 / D-50-020 / D-50-021** held at **P1**. Reviewer challenge: "These are surface-authoring gaps, not unbuildability." Rebuttal: a matrix cell without surface authoring is exactly an unbuildable feature — quorum is gated, but the action's idempotency, audit linkage, customer notification, state machine, and rollback path are all undeclared. P1 stands.
- **D-50-017** held at **P1**. Considered demotion to P2. Rejected because ContestRecord adjudication reverses billing — the same authority that requires quorum on the downstream reversal action (§50.3.2 line 38816) is solo on the upstream decision. The asymmetry is a buildability defect. P1 stands.
- **D-50-018 / D-50-019** held at **P1**. Considered P0 for D-50-018 (GDPR Article 13/14 violation). Rejected because the 14-day window + P1 page is an acknowledged escalation; the gap is the absence of the customer-disclosure horizon, not a complete absence of disclosure. P1 stands.
- **D-50-006 vs Phase 43 D-43-002 overlap.** D-43-002 catalogs the §43 side (capability not in Appendix J). D-50-006 catalogs the §50 side (no surface authored). Same root cause, different surfaces; complementary defects; both retained.
- **D-50-001 vs Phase 43 D-43-002 overlap.** D-43-002 is the §43-side matrix-coverage gap. D-50-001 is the §50-side matrix-closure violation (§50.10 / §50.11 / §50.13 / §50.14 don't extend the matrix). Different; both retained.
- **D-50-013 / D-50-016 / D-50-023 / D-50-026 / D-50-033 / D-50-035 / D-50-040 P2 challenges.** Each held at P2: ambiguity resolvable by a thoughtful engineer but not the same across two readers. No demotions.

No defects demoted from P0. No findings withdrawn.

### Phase 46 Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read 22 findings as a hostile reviewer. Key severity tests:

- **D-46-005 (P1, console firewall absent).** Considered demotion-to-P0-trigger by Rule (a) — "breaks the buyer/seller console firewall." Rebuttal: §46 silence on test coverage is documentation absence, not an active firewall break. The active break is at §1.3 / §4.7 / §27.10 surfaces themselves; §46 is the test contract that would *catch* a regression. P1 by tiebreaker stands.
- **D-46-006 (P1, DSAR/GDPR absent).** Same framing as D-46-005 by Rule (c). P1 stands.
- **D-46-013 (P1, AIWallet/OutcomeContract/Cost-Base testing absent).** Same framing by Rule (d). P1 stands.
- **D-46-010 (P1, feature-flag Solo-wallet conflict).** Considered P0 by Rule (d) — "billing surface ambiguous in a way that allows revenue leakage." Rebuttal: the actual entitlement is at §34.8 (authoritative); §46.4 documentation drift does not change runtime enforcement. P1 stands.
- **D-46-020 (P2, security testing absent).** Considered P1 by Rule (regulatory / PII exposure). Rebuttal: §45 Privacy & Security authors the control contract; §46 absence is a test-strategy gap, not a control gap. P2 stands.

No demotions. No revisions to severity classification.

### Phase V12 Closure Path

The 8 inherited P0 defects map to two distinct remediation packs:

1. **§43 Retirement Pack** — closes D-43-001 through D-43-006 in a single structural edit. §43 is superseded by §50 per the §50.1 preamble; the simplest remediation is to retire §43.1–§43.5 prose to a one-paragraph retirement banner that hard-routes admin-tooling implementation to §50. Per PHASE43 coupling analysis: D-43-001 / -002 / -007 / -018 close via the retirement banner; D-43-003 / -006 close via §50.4 / §50.2.3 contract enforcement; D-43-004 / -009 close via `admin_audit_log` retirement to §4.6.1.

2. **§50 Plan-Override + §42 Revenue-Metric Pack** — closes D-50-006 + D-42-001. Author §50.X Plan-Tier Manual Override Ops Surface at §50.12 Pricing Admin authoring fidelity. Author the missing revenue-affecting alarms in §42.2 (AIOperation acceptance, AIWallet debit, OutcomeContract settlement, Stripe meter-event submit, Solo per-eval / per-bid charge) bound to per-service SLOs in §44.1 / §44.2.

### Phase HM Severity Roll-Up

0 P0 / 6 P1 / 8 P2 / 2 P3 = 16 net-new defects.

The six P1s cluster into three categories:
- **Definitional / contract integrity (3):** D-HM-001 (Hero Moment exit ambiguity); D-HM-003 + D-HM-004 (PostHog event payload schema drift between §48.8.3 inline and Appendix G §48.8.8).
- **Coverage gap (1):** D-HM-002 (buyer-side Hero Moment missing entirely — the audit prompt's "buyer-side + seller-side" coverage requirement).
- **User recovery (1):** D-HM-006 (no abandonment re-engagement path).
- **Solo-tier completeness (1):** D-HM-009 (Solo-tier Hero Moment cohort and SLO not separately specified).

The eight P2s are taxonomy reconciliation, naming-collision, and cohort-coverage items resolvable at v7.1.1. The two P3s are glossary completion (D-HM-013) and consolidated-surface-doc hygiene (D-HM-016).
