### Phase 13V Severity Roll-Up

0 P0 / 6 P1 / 19 P2 / 1 P3 = 26 net-new defects.

The six P1s cluster into four categories:

- **STRUCTURAL coverage gaps (2):** D-13V-001 (§48.2 L1–L10 unaudited); D-13V-002 (§48.4 Anti-Spam unaudited).
- **M16 buyer growth loop (2):** D-13V-004 (same-domain enforcement temporal ordering); D-13V-008 (M16 funnel definition absent).
- **Hero Moment failure construction (2):** D-13V-022 (Firecrawl-outage instrumentation gap); D-13V-023 (Bootstrap allowance compensation contract).

The 19 P2s cluster into edge-case acceptance criteria (10), numerical singleton drift (3), surface/engine mapping verification (2), instrumentation cross-reference (2), enum / retention / authored_extension (3). The 1 P3 is the L1 attribution-window boundary inclusivity (D-13V-026).

### Phase 14.1 Roll-Up

- **Severity distribution:** 4 P1 (D-14.1-001, D-14.1-002, D-14.1-003, D-14.1-010) / 6 P2 (D-14.1-004 through D-14.1-009) / 0 P3 / 0 P0.
- **Class distribution:** 10 × `consistency_drift`. No P0 numerical-singleton drift; no firewall / DSAR / residency / RBAC defects (the BPS v3 walk is narrative-vs-spec scope, not engineering-correctness scope).
- **Authoritative resolution:** All 10 defects resolve **per CLAUDE.md §2 source-of-truth — Master Spec wins.** 9 defects recommend extending the spec to cover the BPS v3 commitments; 1 defect (D-14.1-008) opens a Critical Question with two resolution paths (spec-mechanism authoring vs BPS-narrative amendment).
- **AE Ledger queue:** 7 of 10 defects emit Authored Extensions requiring entry in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` before v7.1.1 stamp. Registered post-remediation rows: D-14.1-001 (Scenario D), D-14.1-002 (90-day Solo trial), D-14.1-003 (Solo upgrade-CTA throttling trigger), and D-14.1-010 (Pricing Engineering AE-12 through AE-18, paired with D-14.2-004). Remaining AE-producing open defects: D-14.1-007 (SR v2-watermarking grandfathering) and D-14.1-009 (3 surface-hide-list extensions). D-14.1-004 / D-14.1-005 / D-14.1-006 / D-14.1-008 are Finance-scorecard / Decisions-ledger items (no AE row required).
- **CI gate additions:** Registered post-remediation validators / assertions: `solo_trial_one_per_org_lifetime` (D-14.1-002), consolidated Buyer/Seller gate `solo_upgrade_cta_threshold_3_events_30d_subscription_immediate_per_eval_bid` (D-14.1-003 / D-14.2-003), and the §34.17.4 `pricing_engineering_coverage` assertion over AE-1 through AE-18 (D-14.1-010 / D-14.2-004). Remaining recommended deploy-time validators: `selection_report_watermark_effective_at_single_source` (D-14.1-007); `solo_surface_hides_plan_tier_matrix_pulse_health_score_cohort_taxonomy` (D-14.1-009).
- **Spec-side remediation cost:** ~7 spec sections require authoring or extension (§13.11, §34.5, §34.9, §34.17.1.b, §34.18.5, §34.18.6, §44.6) plus 2 sections require new Solo-mode replacement surfaces authored from scratch (§16 "what to do this week" panel; §13.5 / §13.12 Solo email-domain auto-assignment heuristic).
- **Halt-rule policy:** Audit prompt halt rule "ANY DRIFT IS P1 consistency_drift" applied pragmatically (precedent from PHASE34.PXC walk): structural narrative-vs-spec gap rendering a BPS v3 commitment unbuildable as written escalates to P1; narrative-only or instrumentation-only coverage drift remains P2. Strict-interpretation conversion would escalate D-14.1-004 through D-14.1-009 to P1 (10 P1 total); the strict list is recorded for v7.1.1 backlog completeness but recommendation stands at the pragmatic-interpretation severity assignment.

### Phase 14.2 Roll-Up

- **Severity distribution:** 5 P1 (D-14.2-001, D-14.2-002, D-14.2-003, D-14.2-004, D-14.2-005) / 5 P2 (D-14.2-006, D-14.2-007, D-14.2-008, D-14.2-009, D-14.2-010) / 1 P3 (D-14.2-011) / 0 P0.
- **Class distribution:** 11 × `consistency_drift`. No P0 numerical-singleton drift; no firewall / DSAR / residency / RBAC defects (the SPS v3 walk is narrative-vs-spec scope, not engineering-correctness scope — D-V6-001 Marketplace Discovery firewall P0 is pre-filed in Phase 34.16 V6, not Phase 14.2).
- **Authoritative resolution:** All 11 defects resolve **per CLAUDE.md §2 source-of-truth — Master Spec wins.** 10 defects recommend extending the spec to cover the SPS v3 commitments; 1 defect (D-14.2-011) recommends a SPS v3 narrative edit (citation drift; no spec change). No Critical Question opens in this walk (unlike Phase 14.1's D-14.1-008).
- **AE Ledger queue:** 6 of 11 defects emit Authored Extensions requiring entry in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` before v7.1.1 stamp. Registered post-remediation rows: D-14.2-001 (Seller Solo Scenario D), D-14.2-002 (90-day Seller Solo trial), D-14.2-003 (Seller Solo upgrade-CTA throttling trigger), and D-14.2-004 (§34.17.1.b AE-17 + AE-18, paired with D-14.1-010 AE-12 through AE-16). D-14.2-005 (4 Conversion Moments) is now remediated as a §48.1.7 table + enum extension and does not emit an AE. Remaining AE-producing open defects: D-14.2-008 (3 surface-hide-list extensions) and D-14.2-009 (KB v2-cutover grandfathering). D-14.2-006 / D-14.2-007 / D-14.2-010 / D-14.2-011 are scorecard / debrief / cite-drift items (no AE row required).
- **CI gate additions:** Registered post-remediation validators / assertions: `solo_trial_one_per_org_lifetime` (D-14.2-002, shared with D-14.1-002), consolidated Buyer/Seller gate `solo_upgrade_cta_threshold_3_events_30d_subscription_immediate_per_eval_bid` (D-14.2-003 / D-14.1-003), and the §34.17.4 `pricing_engineering_coverage` assertion over AE-1 through AE-18 (D-14.2-004 / D-14.1-010). Remaining recommended deploy-time validators: `solo_plan_matrix_surfacing_upgrade_context_only` (D-14.2-008); `solo_kb_governance_weekly_notification_template_parity` (D-14.2-008); `seller_kb_v2_cutover_grandfathering_single_source` (D-14.2-009); `seller_bid_close_debrief_win_loss_solo_starter_copy_parity` (D-14.2-010).
- **Spec-side remediation cost:** Remaining open Phase 14.2 spec-side work is concentrated in §22.20 / §34.6 / §34.13.4 / §44.6.1 / §49.1.7 plus new Loops.so template authoring across 4 templates (`tpl_solo_kb_governance_weekly_notification`, `tpl_seller_bid_close_debrief_win_solo_starter`, `tpl_seller_bid_close_debrief_loss_solo_starter`, plus the existing `pro_trial_seat.auto_downgraded` template extension for contextual Solo-vs-Starter CTA per D-14.2-007). §34.9 / §34.17.1.b / §34.18.6 / §48.1.7 were remediated in the 2026-06-21 P1 passes.
- **Halt-rule policy:** Audit prompt halt rule "ANY DRIFT IS P1 consistency_drift" applied pragmatically (precedent from PHASE34.PXC + PHASE14.1 walks): structural narrative-vs-spec gap rendering a SPS v3 commitment unbuildable as written escalates to P1; narrative-only or instrumentation-only coverage drift remains P2; cosmetic citation drift remains P3. Strict-interpretation conversion would escalate D-14.2-006 through D-14.2-010 to P1 (10 P1 total; 1 P3); the strict list is recorded for v7.1.1 backlog completeness but recommendation stands at the pragmatic-interpretation severity assignment.

- **v7.1.1 stamp gate inherits:** D-14.2-001 through D-14.2-011 closure; already remediated as of 2026-06-21: D-14.2-001 / D-14.2-002 / D-14.2-003 / D-14.2-004 / D-14.2-005. ### Phase 14.4 Counterfactual Pass

For each defect, three realistic failure modes considered:

1. **D-14.4-001 (Heading 3 / 4 undefined).** (a) Engineering picks the wrong font size (e.g., reads "Heading 4" as 14px Body) — visual hierarchy of Modal title vs. body collapses; Modal title becomes indistinguishable from Modal body. (b) Designer authors a new Heading 4 in Figma (16px / weight 400) without coordinating with Master Spec — Figma-to-code Tokens Studio export pushes a stale value; Modal title renders with wrong weight. (c) Accessibility audit fails: A-08 (semantic HTML h1–h6) expects the Modal title to map to an `<h2>` or `<h3>` element; without a typography role bound to a heading level, the HTML semantic structure drifts. All three resolved by the recommendation: either rewrite to cite existing roles (option b) or register the new roles in §2.1 with concrete pixel values.
2. **D-14.4-006 (8px vs 4px helper-gap).** (a) Engineering implements 8px per UX §5.2.13 — every form field across the app renders with double the helper-gap; layout density drops; mobile responsive layouts (per UX §3.4 tablet < 1024px) overflow. (b) QA writes a Playwright test expecting `--input-helper-gap` from §3.6.1 token; test fails against the 8px implementation; engineering revert vs. spec edit becomes a coin-flip. (c) Tokens Studio Figma export contains 4px (per Master Spec §3.6.1) but the implementation uses 8px (per UX §5.2.13); Figma-to-code parity check fails. Resolved by rewriting UX §5.2.13 to cite `--input-helper-gap` and adding the regex-detector validator.
3. **D-14.4-009 (Dark Mode token values absent).** (a) Engineering ships dark-mode CSS with no tokens defined; the entire app renders as light-mode-on-dark-background (text on white background within dark surrounding) — unusable. (b) Designer authors dark-mode in Figma in isolation without Master Spec coordination; per-token contrast verification (UX §11.6 A-01 ≥ 4.5:1) is never run; multiple tokens ship below WCAG; legal accessibility-compliance exposure. (c) A user with `prefers-color-scheme: dark` opens the app; Side Peek renders with `--color-bg-elevated: #FFFFFF` because no dark-mode override exists; the side peek is white-on-white invisible against the dark page background. Resolved by authoring the dark-mode palette table in UX §2.2 + WCAG verification via Axe-core in `ux_token_drift_check`.
4. **D-14.4-012 (A/B/C/D vs FM/PM/DNM/EX).** (a) Color-blind simulation QA test reads AC A-09's `A/B/C/D` and produces a test fixture with grade-A through grade-D DOM markers; test passes trivially against fixture that doesn't reflect production; production color-blind regression slips. (b) A new engineer joins the team, reads UX §11.6, and refactors GradeBadge to expose `A/B/C/D` props — production breaks across §4 / §11 / §13 / Appendix J consumers. (c) Customer-success documentation reads `A/B/C/D` and publishes external-facing documentation with the wrong vocabulary; sellers and buyers see grade-A in docs but FM in product. Resolved by rewriting AC A-09 to cite FM/PM/DNM/EX + Appendix J + adding the regex-detector to the CI gate.

### Phase 14.4 Self-Challenge Pass

Re-read findings as hostile staff engineer.

- **D-14.4-001 / -003 / -004 (undefined tokens P2).** Hostile reviewer: *"These are 'token cited but not defined' findings — every one is structurally a P1 'feature unbuildable as written' under the Severity Definitions rule. Why P2?"* Counter: each defect has TWO buildable resolution paths (option a — register the new token; option b — rewrite to cite an existing token). A P1 is reserved for cases where no buildable resolution exists; P2 is the correct severity when "a thoughtful staff engineer could resolve, but the resolution is not the *same* across two readers." Strict-interpretation P1 list recorded; pragmatic-interpretation P2 stands. (D-14.4-001 and D-14.4-010 are the closest to P1; recorded in the strict list.)
- **D-14.4-006 (helper-gap 4px vs 8px P2).** Hostile reviewer: *"Master Spec §3.6.1 is authoritative; UX v2 §5.2.13 is wrong; this is a P1 numerical_singleton drift, not P2."* Counter: the precedent set by D-AS-001 / D-AS-002 / D-AS-006 (Phase 1 numerical-singleton drifts) is P1 for pricing-relevant numerics (dollar figures, AI budgets) where the engineering blast radius is revenue / legal. The helper-gap drift is visually consequential but not revenue-blocking; per the Severity Definitions rule "P1 = missing field-level schema, missing acceptance criteria, missing state machine, missing error code, missing webhook contract, missing plan-gating row in §5.11/§34.1/§39, missing retention/DSAR/residency clause, conflicting numerical singleton between Master Spec and a companion strategy doc, or surface introduced without an Appendix-M row" — the listed conflicting-numerical-singleton applies to companion strategy docs (BPS / SPS), and the audit prompt's classification rule for UX v2 drift is "P2 typically; P1 if a UX contract is unimplementable as written." The 8px-vs-4px drift is buildable (either value renders a usable form); P2 stands.
- **D-14.4-008 (z-index 50 collision P2).** Hostile reviewer: *"Toast + AmendmentBanner at same z-index is a stacking conflict that breaks a primary UX contract — should be P1."* Counter: the practical impact is undefined stacking order between Toast and Banner; both render; user can dismiss either; no functionality is lost. The visual layering glitch is a P2 ambiguity ("the resolution is not the same across two readers") rather than a P1 unbuildable. P2 stands.
- **D-14.4-009 (Dark Mode palette absent P2).** Hostile reviewer: *"An entire visual-design mode (dark mode) is structurally undefined; this is a P1 'surface introduced without an Appendix-M row' equivalent."* Counter: dark mode is referenced in UX §2.2 ("All color tokens have dark-mode equivalents") and Master Spec §3.11 authoritatively rules dark mode parity — the contract exists, only the concrete token values are missing from UX v2 §2.2. Master Spec §3.11 is the canonical home; UX §2.2 is the paired-mirror surface; the gap is a paired-mirror coverage gap, not an absence-of-contract gap. P2 stands.
- **D-14.4-012 (A/B/C/D vs FM/PM/DNM/EX P2).** Hostile reviewer: *"AC A-09 is unbuildable as written — any QA engineer authoring an Axe-core test from A-09 produces a test against a fixture that doesn't exist. P1."* Counter: the AC IS unbuildable as written verbatim, but the resolution is unambiguous (replace `A/B/C/D` with `FM/PM/DNM/EX` per Appendix J + §2.7). The hostile-reviewer test "does the AC produce the wrong build" is positive — but the recovery is trivial (a single regex-replace). Under the Severity Definitions tiebreaker "default to P1 if a junior engineer would build the wrong thing," D-14.4-012 is the closest to P1 in this cluster. Pragmatic P2 stands because the regex-detector validator forecloses the failure mode; strict P1 recorded.

No severity revisions on re-read.

- **Phase 14.4 BROAD (zero P1 / P2 open in UX-v2 ↔ Master Spec scope):** **FAIL pre-remediation.** 0 P1 + 12 P2 open. ### Phase AE Counterfactual Pass

For the AE ratification process itself, three realistic failure modes enumerated and the spec checked against each. Detailed in `_audit/PHASE_AE_FINDINGS.md → §11 Counterfactual Pass`:

- **An owner ratifies an AE that has since been V11-amended in place** (e.g., Engineering signs AE-14.18.1-01 without realizing the 122-row catalog assertion is V11-derived). Without a `dependency_blockers` column, the ratification race is plausible. Surfaces at D-AE-011.
- **A superseded AE remains in the queue and an owner ratifies the now-stale body** (e.g., Pricing signs AE-12.4-DEF-06 after the V2 remediation already landed §34.2.4). Without `superseded` transitions, this is plausible. Surfaces at D-AE-007.
- **v7.1.1 stamps with AE-V11-04 still a stub.** The stub claims Phase 11.5 will run; if Phase 11.5 slips, the stamp gate either bypasses (silent process drift, repeating the v7.1.0 stamp issue at D-AE-013) or blocks indefinitely. Surfaces at D-AE-015.

### Phase V711 Halt-Rule Evaluation

- Zero P0 firewall-leakage / DSAR / billing / CI-gate-runtime-unwireable defects: **PASS**. D-V711-009 (`solo_deadline_countdown_renders_in_user_timezone` §M.5 row absence) was assessed against Severity Rule P0 ("CI gate runtime-unwireable as written") and held at P1 (upgraded from initial P2 in self-challenge pass) because the gate is named in spec body but not in catalog — the runtime wiring is blocked, not the spec-binding contract.
- Zero P0 scope-leakage / consistency-drift: **PASS**. D-V711-008 (v7.1.1 backlog scope-leak across 27 artifacts) was assessed against Severity Rule P1 ("feature unbuildable as written") and held at P1 because a stamp executor working from RECONCILIATION alone would mechanically ship with ~370 items unresolved.
- **Verdict.** HALT not triggered. 8 P1 + 8 P2 = 16 defects route into v7.1.1 stamp-gate backlog-discipline pack.

### Phase V711 Self-Challenge Pass Revisions

- D-V711-009 initial severity P2 (documentation_gap); revised P1 (ci_gate) per Severity Rule P1 ("missing CI gate referenced in `Build_Execution_Strategy.md` runtime-unwireable as written"). Gate is named in §2.8.7 AC #5 but absent from `§M.5.4` catalog → runtime wiring cannot proceed against a non-existent catalog row.
- D-V711-016 added in self-challenge pass (REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md last-updated banner stale); not present in initial scratch findings. Cosmetic but worth filing for audit hygiene.
- Aggregate count drift from initial scratch (15 defects) to final ledger (16 defects) is the result of the self-challenge addition; severity reclassification on D-V711-009 (P2 → P1) further tightens the severity distribution toward the rule-based contract.

### Phase V711 Counterfactual Pass

Three realistic failure modes for the v7.1.1 stamp gate (per `_audit/V711_READINESS.md` §9):

1. **AE ratification queue blocks indefinitely.** ~75 pending AE rows distributed across 8+ sign-off roles (Engineering Lead, Security Lead, Privacy Officer, Founder, GTM, Sales Ops, Finance, Design Director, KB Lead, Marketing). No ratification SLA in the release-gate policy. **Spec response.** Not addressed in this audit; recommend AE Ledger policy amendment to specify ratification SLA per program section.
2. **CI gate runtime wiring slips past v7.1.1.** M02.3 / M11.3 / M21.3 / M24.3 packs are engineering implementation, not spec authoring; runtime_status field can only transition `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` → `runtime_active` after the pack lands. **Spec response.** Addressed by D-V711-007 (per-gate AC) + D-V711-011 (per-gate pack assignment).
3. **Phase 11.5 M.1 Backfill discovers new defects.** ~135 M.1 row authorings will inevitably surface companion-doc anchor errors, tier-visibility cell ambiguities, engine-concept naming inconsistencies. **Spec response.** Phase 11.5 should budget same-session remediation pass at 50% margin (Audit_Prompts.md adversarial review pattern).
